To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
domain-specific psychological need satisfaction predicts the self-concordance of people's goals.
the extent to which a person’s goals are self-concordant is influenced by how much psychological need satisfaction the person experiences in the domain in which the goal is set.
Domain-related need satisfaction is a strong predictor of the extent to which goals in this domain are self-concordant.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of domain-specific psychological need satisfaction in goal self-concordant choice and internalization.
the role of need satisfaction in the process of goal setting and goal attainment.
the question of why people adopt self-congruent goals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this paper provides evidence that the more a person is satisfied in a particular domain, the more likely he or she will set goals that are in line with his or her personal interests, and that this is due to the fact that in need-satisfing domains people are more likely to choose self-concordant options and to internalize these options.

this research shows that the more people experience need satisfaction in a particular domain, the more likely they will set self-concordant and internalized goals in that domain, and the more successful they are likely to be in achieving them.
need satisfaction in a particular domain is a strong predictor of the self-concordance of goals adopted in that domain.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
people are more likely to adopt self-concordent goals in need-satisfiying domains.
the more need satisfying a domain is, the more likely a person will set self-concordant, and therefore more attainable, goals in that domain.

self-concordance is an important factor in the success of goal pursuit, and the present research shows that self-concordent goals are more likely when goals are set in domains that provide need satisfaction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the goals we set are not random.
goal choice is not a simple matter of choosing the goal that you think is best.
people are more likely to set self-concordant and self-congruent goals when they are in a need-satisfying domain.
